claims.text: The Royal Opera House is one of the world's great performance venues and is often referred to simply as 'Covent Garden'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The first theatre on this site was built in 1732 and actually served primarily as a playhouse for its first hundred years.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The legendary composer George Frideric Handel began staging his first season of operas here shortly after and wrote many masterpieces specifically for this venue.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The current building is actually the third theatre to stand here, as the previous two were destroyed by disastrous fires in 1808 and 1856.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The beautiful historic facade and the massive 2,256-seat auditorium both date to 1858, though much of the rest was rebuilt in the 1990s.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: While there is no formal dress code, visitors are advised to dress smartly to avoid disapproving looks from other attendees.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: If you want to catch a show, know that at least 65 tickets for each performance are held back for in-person sales starting at 10AM.
claims.subject: self
